newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian SGB not looking to up Sagem stake.
newsitem.headline: Belgian SGB not looking to up Sagem stake.

text.p: Belgian holding company Ste Generale de Belgique (SGB) said on Tuesday it would not look to increase its stake in French electronics group Sagem SA when shares in Sagem's controlling holding company come up for sale next year.

"As far as we are concerned, we are happy with 20 percent...it does not mean we will be so forever, but for now we don't plan to go higher," SGB chief executive officer Philippe Liotier told a news conference on SGB's interim 1996 earnings.
SGB owns 20 percent of Coficem, the employee-owned holding company that controls 53 percent of Sagem's voting rights.

Prior to SGB's multi-billion Belgian franc purchase this month of shares in Belgian utility group Tractebel, analysts had speculated the company might be tempted to increase its stake once, for technical and fiscal reasons, a number of Coficem shares come up for sale in 1997.
Liotier said, however, it was unlikely that any Coficem/Sagem shares would come on to the market to be bought by someone else.
"There is sufficient cash within Coficem to recycle the holding. It's not foreseen that there will be any additional flow of Coficem to the market," Liotier said.
SGB on Monday completed a 49 billion Belgian franc purchase of 24.47 percent of Tractebel held by companies linked to rival Belgian holding Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA.
SGB will also offer other Tractebel shareholders the opportunity to sell their shares in a public offer running from October 9 to 30.
To finance the Tractebel acquisition, SGB has taken on 72 billion Belgian francs in new bank debt.
SGB is 62 percent-owned by France'e Cie. de Suez.
